title: Research Assistant – Health Monitoring System for Diesel Engines
experience: B.Tech / M.Tech (Mechanical/Automobile with specialization in IC Engines)
education: B.Tech in Mechanical or Automobile Engineering (specialization in IC Engines) or M.Tech in Mechanical/Automobile Engineering with specialization in IC Engines
description: Join the Engine Health Monitoring Systems team to develop strap-on multi-sensor monitoring solutions for diesel engine subsystems, focusing on data acquisition, baseline & fault modelling, and algorithmic health assessment.
responsibilities: Identify and define appropriate sensor deployment locations on diesel engines (combustion, exhaust, cooling, lubrication) for non-intrusive strap-on sensors.
Select suitable sensors (temperature, pressure, vibration, ultrasonic) considering environment (heat, vibration, oil mist), mounting feasibility, repeatability, and data quality.
Design and fabricate (or coordinate fabrication of) attach-and-detach mounting mechanisms for sensors while the engine remains mounted in the vehicle.
Create detailed fault-mapping trees and diagrams correlating measured parameter changes (temperature, pressure, vibration, ultrasonic) to subsystem/component health states or fault conditions.
Devise experimental plans to acquire baseline data under different loads/speeds and generate labelled datasets by introducing controlled simulated faults (one at a time).
Develop testing protocols (sampling rates, operating envelopes, sensor calibration, safety and environmental correction procedures).
Acquire and log test data, ensure preprocessing readiness and hand-over to the software/algorithm development team.
Provide domain-expert support to software/algorithm teams on diesel engine fundamentals, subsystem behaviour, and fault signatures in sensor signals.
Maintain documentation: sensor mounting reports, experimental logs, fault-mapping diagrams, protocol documents and data-archive indexing.
Collaborate with cross-functional teams (hardware, sensors, data acquisition, software) to support integration and test phases.
requirements: B.Tech or M.Tech in Mechanical/Automobile Engineering with specialization or strong coursework in IC (internal combustion) engines.
Interest or prior exposure to engine testing, sensors, data-acquisition, condition monitoring or diagnostics is a plus.
Hands-on attitude: experience mounting sensors, working on test benches, and familiarity with mechanical and sensor hardware.
Comfortable with signal/data handling and basic scripting (MATLAB or Python desirable).
Good communication skills (English and/or Hindi) and ability to produce clear documentation.
preferred: Prior experience with diesel engine testing or condition monitoring projects.
Familiarity with data acquisition systems, DAQ configuration and basic signal preprocessing.
Experience preparing experimental protocols and labeling datasets.
offer: Duration: 12 months initially (extendable to a second year subject to review and project funding)
Fully on-site (Pune) — occasional work during engine test runs outside regular hours as needed
Travel may be required to engine test workshops, vehicle installation sites or sensor mounting locations
Consolidated fellowship (no additional benefits unless specified separately)
Start date: Immediate / As soon as possible
Career progression: Candidates demonstrating exceptional performance may be offered a regular position in the Electronic and Mechanical Division after one year
How to Apply: Email your resume to careers@guardinger.in
